class spike_swarm_sim.controllers.controller.RobotController(controller_owner=None)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.controllers.controller.Controller

Base class for Robot Controllers. Any Controller devoted to the management of robot actions must inherit from this class. The controller functionality must be implemented within the overwritten Controller.step method. In order to use them, sensors and actuators must be enabled by the controller first (controllers normally use only a subset of all available sensors and actuators). Sensor can be activated through either add_sensor to enable them one by one or using add_sensors_from_dict, to activate all at once. Similarly, actuators can be included using either add_actuator or add_actuators_from_dict.

Parameters:

controller_owner (Robot) – Instance of the robot owning the controller.
Variables:
  • enabled_sensors (dict) – dict with storing the sensors enabled by the controller. It maps sensor reference names to a dict with the paramters of the sensor.
  • enabled_actuators (dict) – dict with storing the actuators enabled by the controller. It maps sensor reference names to a dict with the paramters of the actuators.
add_sensors_from_dict(robot_sensors)[source]¶

Add the sensors that the controller can make use of in the form of a python dict. The dict structure must be {“sensor_name” : sensor_params}. Notice that, at this point, the sensor is not yet activated by the robot. In order to activate it, the robot object has to be created afterwards or the reset method of the robot has to be called.

Parameters:robot_sensors (dict) – dict with all the sensors to be activated, mapping the sensor reference name and another dict (subdict) with the sensor parameters.

Example:

>>> robot_sensors = {'distance_sensor' : {'n_sectors' : 8, 'range' : 1}}
add_actuators_from_dict(robot_actuators)[source]¶

Add the actuators that the controller can make use of in the form of a python dict. Notice that, at this point, the actuator is not yet activated by the robot. In order to activate it, the robot object has to be created afterwards or the reset method of the robot has to be called.

The dict structure must be {“actuator_name” : actuator_params}.

Parameters:robot_actuators (dict) – dict with all the actuators to be activated, mapping the actuator reference name and another dict (subdict) with the actuator parameters.

Example:

>>> robot_actuators = {'joint_velocity_actuator' : {'joint_ids' : [0,1], 'max_velocity' : 10}}
add_sensor(sensor_name, sensor_params)[source]¶

Adds a single sensor to the enabled sensors by the robot. Notice that, at this point, the sensor is not yet activated by the robot. In order to activate it, the robot object has to be created afterwards or the reset method of the robot has to be called.

Parameters:
  • sensor_name (dict) – reference name of the sensor to be enabled.
  • sensor_name – dict with the parameters of the sensor to be enabled.
add_actuator(actuator_name, actuator_params)[source]¶

Adds a single sensor to the enabled actuators by the robot. Notice that, at this point, the sensor is not yet activated by the robot. In order to activate it, the robot object has to be created afterwards or the reset method of the robot has to be called.

Parameters:
  • actuator_name (str) – reference name of the actuator to be enabled.
  • actuator_params (dict) – dict with the parameters of the actuator to be enabled.

spike_swarm_sim.controllers.basic_obstacle_avoider module¶

class spike_swarm_sim.controllers.basic_obstacle_avoider.BasicObstacleAvoider(*args, sensitivity=0.15, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.controllers.controller.RobotController

Controller devoted to the obstacle avoidance task. This means that the controller will read from the distance sensor, process the measurements and return joint velocity actions required to avoid colliding with any other tangible entity. This controller is currently hard coded for the Epuck robot.

Parameters:sensitivity (float) – value in [0, 1] that defines the threshold in the distance sensor reading to interpret an obstacle detection.

spike_swarm_sim.controllers.braitenberg1_controller module¶

class spike_swarm_sim.controllers.braitenberg1_controller.Braitenberg2B(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.controllers.controller.RobotController

Controller based on the Braitenberg vehicle 2B. This vehicle reacts to incoming light by following the light gradient.

step(state, reward=0.0)[source]¶

Method to execute once the controller program. It reads the current light sensor measurement, and plans the action as follows:

\[ \begin{align}\begin{aligned}a_{wr} = \max\{ls_4, ls_5, ls_6, ls_7\}\\a_{wl} = \max\{ls_0, ls_1, ls_2, ls_3\}\end{aligned}\end{align} \]

where :math`a_{wr}` and \(a_{wl}\) are the right and left wheel actions and \(ls_i\) is the light sensor of the \(i\)-th sector. If no light is detected at all, then the actions are :math`a_{wr}=a_{wl}=0.2`.

Parameters:
  • state (dict) – state with the sensor reading. The dict maps the reference name of the sensor to the sensor np.ndarray reading.
  • reward (float) – reward (if any). Not used in this controller.
class spike_swarm_sim.controllers.braitenberg1_controller.Braitenberg2A(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.controllers.controller.RobotController

Controller based on the Braitenberg vehicle 2b. This vehicle reacts to incoming light by escaping from the light source.

step(state, reward=0.0)[source]¶

Method to execute once the controller program. It reads the current light sensor measurement, and plans the action as follows:

\[ \begin{align}\begin{aligned}a_{wl} = \max\{ls_4, ls_5, ls_6, ls_7\}\\a_{wr} = \max\{ls_0, ls_1, ls_2, ls_3\}\end{aligned}\end{align} \]

where :math`a_{wr}` and \(a_{wl}\) are the right and left wheel actions and \(ls_i\) is the light sensor of the \(i\)-th sector. If no light is detected at all, then the actions are :math`a_{wr}=a_{wl}=0.2`.

Parameters:
  • state (dict) – state with the sensor reading. The dict maps the reference name of the sensor to the sensor np.ndarray reading.
  • reward (float) – reward (if any). Not used in this controller.

spike_swarm_sim.controllers.random_movement_controller module¶

class spike_swarm_sim.controllers.random_movement_controller.RandomMovementController(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: spike_swarm_sim.controllers.controller.RobotController

Extremely simple controller that just performs a robot random walk. It requires no sensing information as just samples the velocities of each joint from the uniform distribution \(\mathcal{U}(0, 1)\).

step(state, reward=0.0)[source]¶

Method to execute once the controller program. It samples the velocities of each joint from the uniform distribution \(\mathcal{U}(0, 1)\).

Parameters:
  • state (dict) – state with the sensor reading. The dict maps the reference name of the sensor to the sensor np.ndarray reading. Not used in this controller.
  • reward (float) – reward (if any). Not used in this controller.
